findings.title: Upsampling eligibility uses outer dataset and original request query
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` and the actual `query` to execute, but it calls `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)`. `dataset` is the closure's original dataset, and the helper reads `request.GET['query']`, not the `query` argument. In the dashboard split path this method is invoked with `discover` plus synthesized `errors_only_query`/`transactions_only_query`; a generic query split into errors will not be upsampled, and a transaction-only split derived from a request containing `event.type:error` can be upsampled even though it targets transaction rows. This yields wrong counts and may query sample_weight for transaction data. Pass `scoped_dataset` and the actual query string into the eligibility check.

findings.title: Substring check treats negated and mixed event.type queries as error-only
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the raw query contains the substring `event.type:error`. A query such as `!event.type:error` (which excludes errors) or `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction` is classified as error-only, so `count()` is rewritten to `sum(sample_weight)` for transaction or mixed results. Transaction events have no meaningful sample_weight, so counts are understated or zero. The tests only cover exact positive and transaction-only examples and miss negation/OR cases.

findings.title: upsampled_count drops events whose sample_weight is NULL
findings.body: `upsampled_count` is implemented as `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with no coalesce/default. The new factory helper only sets a sample rate when `contexts.error_sampling.client_sample_rate` exists, and the code explicitly assumes every event has a sample_weight. Any event without a sample rate (older events, unsampled errors, or mixed projects after allowlisting) contributes NULL and is omitted from the sum instead of contributing 1, so allowlisted projects undercount errors. The tests only cover events that have client_sample_rate and would not catch this; the aggregate should use `sum(coalesce(sample_weight, 1))` or equivalent.

findings.title: Top-events ordering still uses unsampled count()
findings.body: When `topEvents` is used, only `timeseries_columns` is rewritten to `upsampled_count()`. The `orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` argument, including any default count ordering, still references the original `count()` aggregation, so Snuba selects the top N groups using raw counts while the response displays upsampled counts. With a large sample-rate skew the endpoint can return the wrong set of top events. The transformed aggregation needs to be applied to orderby/equations as well.

findings.title: Accidental gitlink without .gitmodules
findings.body: This PR adds a gitlink entry named `sentry-repo` pointing at the base commit, but no `.gitmodules` entry or URL is added. A checkout with submodule initialization will fail with `No url found for submodule path 'sentry-repo' in .gitmodules`, and the repository gets an unintended empty submodule. Remove this file/gitlink unless a submodule is genuinely intended.
